text:
alex: Hey team, hitting a reproducible issue with Go SDK v0.9.2 streaming — we get partial/broken JSON from the stream parser and it crashes our consumer.

maria: Which API and deployment? Hosted or Dedicated?

alex: Hosted /v1/chat/stream. Long responses (4k+ tokens) occasionally arrive split mid-JSON object. Example fragments in logs: '{"id":"msg","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello' then next chunk ' world"}}]}' and our parser errors with 'invalid character '\u0077' looking for beginning of value'.

kevin: Do you have a minimal repro program? That error looks like the parser sees a bare token (no opening quote) because the chunk boundary split inside a UTF-8 sequence or inside a string.

alex: Yep, minimal repro below — plain http.Get + bufio.Scanner reading resp.Body and forwarding lines into a json.Unmarshal. Works for small outputs but fails for big ones.

alex: ```go
package main
import (
  "bufio"
  "encoding/json"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  resp, _ := http.Post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream", "application/json", nil)
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  s := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
  for s.Scan() {
    var obj map[string]interface{}
    if err := json.Unmarshal(s.Bytes(), &obj); err != nil {
      fmt.Println("unmarshal error:", err)
      os.Exit(1)
    }
    fmt.Println("got", obj)
  }
}
```

maria: bufio.Scanner has a default max token of 64K, and it splits tokens on newline by default. If the stream is chunked without newline alignment you can easily cut a JSON object in half.

kevin: Also note Go's http/2 framing can split at arbitrary boundaries — you shouldn't assume chunks == logical messages. The SDK used to rely on chunk boundaries, which fails with certain proxies.

alex: Interesting — the SDK in our vendored copy (v0.9.2) has a custom scanner wrapper that expects newline-delimited JSON. We hit two things: (1) upstream chunks don't always include trailing newline, (2) very long sequences exceed the scanner buffer and return 'token too long' in some runs.

sophie: Quick workarounds we've validated: (A) replace bufio.Scanner with json.Decoder and stream-decode via Decoder.Decode on a buffered reader, or (B) call scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 256*1024), 10*1024*1024) to increase token size, and ensure you join partial fragments instead of unmarshalling each Scan() result blindly.

kevin: Repro steps for eng-runtime: 1) run the minimal repro against a long-output prompt (~5000 tokens). 2) Observe unmarshal error or token-too-long. 3) Capture raw bytes of consecutive Read() chunks to confirm chunk boundaries split JSON strings.

alex: We tried the buffer bump and it prevented the token-too-long in our test, but the partial JSON still happens when a boundary splits inside a multi-byte UTF-8 char — Decoder handles that fine.

maria: Can you attach the logs and a small prompt we can use? Also confirm whether the customer is using any proxy or Cloudflare in front of requests.

alex: Logs attached in the ticket (INC-7894). No external proxy, straight request from k8s node. Prompt attached.

support-bot: Ticket INC-7894 created and linked to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

sophie: Action items: 
- eng-runtime to triage: verify sdk stream parser assumption (chunk==message) in v0.9.2 and note failure modes.
- Short-term support: advise customers to use json.Decoder or increase scanner buffer. Provide snippet to set scanner.Buffer.
- Medium-term: release patched Go SDK v0.9.6 that uses a streaming json.Decoder approach and sane default buffer sizes, plus tests against http/2 arbitrary frames.

kevin: I'll own the patch. Plan: replace scanner-based parse with an incremental stateful merge that feeds bytes into a bytes.Buffer and tries to json.Unmarshal on complete objects detected via a small state machine (counting braces and string escapes) to be robust to chunk splits. Add CI test that simulates random TCP chunking.

alex: Thanks — will apply the temp workaround in prod and update the ticket with our deploy window.

maria: Please ping here when v0.9.6 is published so we can notify affected customers. :thumbsup:
